answer_text: URGENT: Refer Immediately to Chandrapuri District Hospital. Bleeding in pregnancy indicates potential placenta praevia or abruption. Call 108 ambulance. Keep woman lying down with elevated legs; do not perform vaginal examination.

Per VIS-1.2: Antenatal Care (ANC) Visits: Calculate gestational age in weeks as of planning date: `(Planning_Date - LMP) / 7`. `ANC_VISIT_1`: 0 to 12 completed weeks. Due if pregnant and no ANC visit recorded yet. `ANC_VISIT_2`: 14 to 26 weeks. Due if pregnant and latest recorded ANC visit was visit 1 (or none).

Per NUT-1.2: MUAC tape is used on the left arm midway between the tip of the shoulder (acromion) and tip of the elbow (olecranon): Red Zone (< 11.5 cm / 115 mm): Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM). Immediate referral or community management protocol required.

URGENT: Refer Immediately to Chandrapuri District Hospital SNCU. Young infant danger signs indicate severe infection, pneumonia, or life-threatening neonatal jaundice. Keep infant warm using skin-to-skin wrapping; call 108.
Yeh vishay ASHA/ANM ke manak protocol ke daayre se bahar hai. Kripya Chandrapuri District Hospital ya nazdeeki PHC ke qualified Medical Officer (doctor) se paramarsh lein.

URGENT: Refer Immediately to Chandrapuri District Hospital. Prolonged labour and cord prolapse are life-threatening delivery emergencies. For cord prolapse: place mother in knee-chest position, wrap cord in sterile cloth, and call 108 immediately.

Per VIS-1.1: Target Community: Chandrapuri Block comprising 6 villages (Amrapur, Belwadi Tola, Kesarganj, Dhanpura, Navagaon Khurd, Sitapahari) served by 5 ASHA workers. Household Dataset: 500 households, 2,234 registered members.

Per NUT-1.3: Press both thumbs firmly but gently on the top of both feet (dorsum of feet) for 3 seconds, then release. If a pit/indentation remains on both feet simultaneously, bilateral pitting edema is present. Bilateral pitting edema indicates Kwashiorkor (severe acute malnutrition) regardless of MUAC measurement, requiring urgent referral.

Per NCD-1.2: Blood pressure measurement on seated individual after 5 minutes of rest: Normal: Systolic BP < 120 mmHg and Diastolic BP < 80 mmHg. Pre-hypertension: Systolic 120-139 mmHg and/or Diastolic 80-89 mmHg. Advise dietary changes, physical activity, and rescreen in 1 year.

URGENT: Refer Immediately to Chandrapuri District Hospital. Severe headache, visual disturbance, and high BP signify impending eclampsia. Administer first dose magnesium sulphate if trained ANM available; call 108 ambulance.

Per CHD-1.1: Classification of dehydration: No Dehydration: Alert, normal eyes, drinks normally, skin pinch goes back immediately. Manage at home with ORS and extra fluids. Some Dehydration: Restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly/thirsty, skin pinch goes back slowly (< 2 seconds). Administer ORS at health sub-centre (approx. 75 ml/kg over 4 hours).
Yeh vishay ASHA/ANM ke manak protocol ke daayre se bahar hai. Kripya Chandrapuri District Hospital ya nazdeeki PHC ke qualified Medical Officer (doctor) se paramarsh lein.

Per IMM-1.2: OPV-1: 2 drops orally. Pentavalent-1 (DPT + Hep B + Hib): 0.5 ml IM, anterolateral aspect of mid-thigh. Rotavirus-1 (RVV): 5 drops orally (or 2.5 ml depending on presentation). Protects against rotavirus diarrhoea. fIPV-1 (Fractional Inactivated Polio Vaccine): 0.1 ml ID on right upper arm.

Per VIS-1.2: Antenatal Care (ANC) Visits: Calculate gestational age in weeks as of planning date: `(Planning_Date - LMP) / 7`. `ANC_VISIT_1`: 0 to 12 completed weeks. Due if pregnant and no ANC visit recorded yet. `ANC_VISIT_2`: 14 to 26 weeks. Due if pregnant and latest recorded ANC visit was visit 1 (or none).

URGENT: Refer Immediately to Chandrapuri District Hospital. Eclampsia and convulsions carry high mortality risk. Call 108. Turn patient onto left side to keep airway clear; never place anything in the mouth; do not give oral liquids.

Per CHD-1.2: Fast Breathing Thresholds (count breaths for 1 full minute when child is calm): Age < 2 months: 60 breaths per minute or faster. Age 2 months to 11 months: 50 breaths per minute or faster. Age 12 months to 59 months: 40 breaths per minute or faster. Classification and Action:

Per VIS-1.3: Each due visit item MUST be assigned an integer priority: Priority 1 (High-Risk and Due/Overdue): Any `HRP_FOLLOWUP` visit. Any infant under 7 days of age requiring HBNC (`HBNC_D1`, `HBNC_D3`, `HBNC_D7`). SAM children due for MUAC screening or follow-up. Overdue visits where the scheduled date is more than 30 days in the past.
Yeh vishay ASHA/ANM ke manak protocol ke daayre se bahar hai. Kripya Chandrapuri District Hospital ya nazdeeki PHC ke qualified Medical Officer (doctor) se paramarsh lein.

URGENT: Refer Immediately to Chandrapuri District Hospital. Convulsions, stiff neck, and unconsciousness in children are general danger signs of meningitis and severe cerebral malaria. Call 108 ambulance immediately.

Per ANC-1.4: Folic Acid: 1 tablet (400 mcg folic acid) daily during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks) to prevent neural tube defects. Iron and Folic Acid (IFA): 1 tablet (100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid) daily starting from the 14th week of pregnancy (second trimester) for a minimum of 180 days during pregnancy and continuing for 180 days postpartum.

URGENT: Refer Immediately to Chandrapuri District Hospital. Severe PPH can lead to hypovolemic shock within hours. Call 108. Perform uterine massage, keep mother warm, and transfer with skilled escort.

Per NUT-1.4: A child aged 6-59 months must be referred to the Chandrapuri NRC under the following conditions: SAM with medical complications (fever, hypothermia, pneumonia, severe diarrhoea, vomiting). SAM with failed Appetite Test (unable or unwilling to eat Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food / energy-dense paste).
Yeh vishay ASHA/ANM ke manak protocol ke daayre se bahar hai. Kripya nazdeeki veterinary doctor (pashu chikitsak) se paramarsh lein.
URGENT: Refer Immediately to Chandrapuri District Hospital. Absent or reduced fetal movements indicate acute fetal distress. Call 108 ambulance for immediate obstetric evaluation.

Per NCD-1.4: Medication Adherence: Reiterate that medicines for BP and diabetes must be taken every single day without interruption, even when feeling well. Salt Intake: Restrict dietary salt to less than 1 teaspoon (< 5 grams) per day. Avoid papad, pickles, and processed snacks.
